newsitem.title: JAPAN: E.Asia Grain- USDA report seen within expectations.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Grain- USDA report seen within expectations.

text.p: Japanese grain traders said on Friday the monthly crop report of the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) was within their expectations, but they will monitor its impact on the market before buying.
Trade houses in Japan have finished covering nearly 95 percent of their U.S. corn requirements for the July-September period of this year.
"(The) USDA's figures were within our expectations. We're not in a hurry to buy corn for the fourth quarter, and want to watch the market impact first," a corn trader in Tokyo said.
Traders in the U.S. said the USDA's supply-demand report was neutral to the market after it left corn carryout unchanged at 909 million bushels.

Corn trading in the CBOT's Project A after hours trading system was relatively subdued in Asianb trade. The July corn futures contract was up by only 1-1/2 U.S. cents at US$2.72-3/4 a bushel at 0935 GMT after trading between $2.73 and $2.71-1/4.
Japan's Food Agency, which is charge of buying wheat, barley and rice, was more worried about the gyrations of the yen against the U.S. dollar.
Dealers said it was forced to postpone some grain import tenders on Thursday due to the yen's plunge against the dollar.
In Taiwan, the Hui Shung Group may tender within two weeks for 8,000 tonnes of corn from either the U.S. or South America.
Delivery will be for late August or early September.
Since the estimates for wheat and corn were little changed, Taiwanese buyers said they do not have to enter the market to buy large quantities of grains in the near term.
South Korean buyers, on the other hand, ignored the USDA report, saying they would may more attention to the USDA quarterly report that will be issued later this month.
